text:
Jonesboro-Hodge High School enrolls 186 students in 2025-26
G. A. Mcgill
Jonesboro-Hodge High School had an enrollment of 186 students in the 2025-26 school year, according to the Louisiana Department of Education.
That was 6.1% fewer than the previous school year, when enrollment was 198 students.
Of students enrolled in the 2025-26 school year, 52.2% were boys and 47.8% were girls.
Most students were Black, representing 67.7% of Jonesboro-Hodge High School's total enrollment.
The school is in Jackson Parish School District, with a central office in Jonesboro.
Statewide, 660,349 students were enrolled in Louisiana in the 2025-26 school year.
Louisiana ranked near the bottom nationally for public school systems, WalletHub's 2026 analysis placed the state 44th among the 50 states and Washington, D.C., with a quality rank of 42 and a safety rank of 48. The analysis compared states across 32 metrics, including student performance, funding, school safety, class size and instructor credentials.
In 2025, Black and White students were the two largest groups reported in Louisiana public schools, according to KIDS COUNT data from Agenda for Children based on Louisiana Department of Education enrollment figures. Black students made up 41.8% of public school enrollment, while White students accounted for 40.2%. Hispanic students accounted for 11.6% of enrollment, continuing a long-term increase in the state's public schools.
Information in this article was obtained from the Kentucky Department of Education. The source data can be found here.
